fact: IOL reports the Cybercrimes Act (2020) as an existing South African law that already provides protections and deals with hacking, online fraud and sharing intimate images without consent; the article is dated 2026-09-16 and gives no other date for the statement.

The authors Fritz and Limpitlaw state that South Africa's Cybercrimes Act criminalises a range of online wrongdoing and provides investigative powers, evidence preservation and international co-operation.
A The Conversation analysis of September 2025 cites the Cybercrimes Act 19 of 2020 as a law that criminalises electronic publication of intimate private images without consent.
The Lesotho Times, citing a SADC Parliamentary Forum and Equality Now brief, says South Africa's Cybercrimes Act makes sharing intimate images without consent a crime.
